correctness.rationale: On the prescribed equal-weight Hardy Laurent basis, direct multiplication yields the exact rational cross-commutator coefficient; the nonzero singular values are its values because the output shift has distinct columns. The three logistic denominators prove strict logarithmic concavity with vanishing tails. Every superlevel set is one bounded interval, giving universal count discrepancy at most one under h-lattice sampling. Layer cake yields the all-p bound. Local uniform convergence with a parameter-uniform exponential envelope gives the moving-degree limits and norm/top-count limits. Substitution and partial-fraction integration give the exact H2 coefficient, including the continuous diagonal limit. Rational identity tests (5,292), numerical integral/symmetry tests (30), and lattice checks (10) passed; these finite tests are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The diagonal/self-commutator unit-error counting formula and the fixed-Laurent-polynomial exact mixed coefficients are both earlier results and are expressly excluded from novelty claims. The final theorem treats unequal degrees, both varying at inverse annulus thickness, and gives a two-parameter nonnormal singular-value distribution, finite-width all-Schatten/level-counting estimates uniform across both degrees, and explicit two-variable Hilbert--Schmidt crossover. Neither the full motivating Toeplitz product paper nor either inspected published spectral paper supplies or directly implies this regime. Relevant published-finding corpus/source searches and own-history comparisons found no dominating statement. Novelty is best-knowledge and not independently certified.
residual_risks: An older equivalent unilateral/bilateral weighted-shift or Hankel cross-product formula could already imply the two-parameter result.
The finite-width constant-one estimate is elementary lattice counting once strict log-concavity is known; it is not claimed as a novel abstract theorem.
Some historical annular spectral literature was accessible only as abstracts, not as full papers; the originality assessment is not an exhaustive priority certification.

value.rationale: The natural two-power commutator [M_{z^m}*,M_{z^n}] measures adjoint-multiplicativity failure and is genuinely nonnormal for unequal degrees. Its two jointly growing monomial scales model distinct spectral boundary layers that fixed-polynomial semiclassical limits exclude. Determining the entire two-parameter continuum singular-value law together with a radius/degree-uniform finite discrepancy, every Schatten quasi-norm and an explicit second-moment constant is a complete natural quantitative invariant, not an arbitrary small parameter increment. The general matrix-band identity and diagonal special case are expressly not sold as new; neither is the elementary lattice-rounding lemma.
